propositions.text: Applicants are Nigerian citizens seeking judicial review of RAD decision dated May 23, 2017.
propositions.quote: The Applicants, citizens of Nigeria, seek judicial review of a decision of the Refugee Appeal Division of the Immigration and Refugee Board [the RAD], dated May 23, 2017 [the Decision],

propositions.text: RAD found Applicants were neither convention refugees nor persons in need of protection under Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.
propositions.quote: which found that they were neither convention refugees nor persons in need of protection pursuant to the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27,

propositions.text: RAD found Applicants had a viable Internal Flight Alternative within Nigeria.
propositions.quote: because they had a viable Internal Flight Alternative [IFA] within Nigeria.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Applicants seek judicial review of RAD decision finding they were not refugees or in need of protection due to a viable IFA in Nigeria.

propositions.text: Application is dismissed for failure to meet onus to show proposed IFA was unreasonable.
propositions.quote: For the reasons that follow, the application is dismissed. The RAD did not err in finding that the Applicants had not met the onus on them to establish that the proposed IFA was not reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the application, finding RAD did not err in concluding Applicants failed to prove the IFA was unreasonable.

propositions.text: Applicants fled Nigeria fearing retribution from family and community for refusing traditional rituals on their children.
propositions.quote: The Applicants, Linda Omono Iyere [Ms. Iyere] and her three children, recount that they fled Nigeria due to a fear of retribution from the family and kinsmen of Mr. Iyere, their husband and father, and of their community members, due to Mr. and Ms. Iyere’s refusal to have their children undergo rituals traditionally performed by that community;

propositions.text: The rituals include Female Genital Mutilation for girls over 13 and symbolic scarring for boys over 15.
propositions.quote: in particular, Female Genital Mutilation [FGM] for girls over the age of thirteen and symbolic scarring for boys over the age of fifteen.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants say they fled Nigeria fearing retribution for refusing traditional rituals including FGM and scarring on their children.

propositions.text: Ms. Iyere and husband told relatives they refused rituals due to Christian faith and husband's negative experiences.
propositions.quote: Ms. Iyere recounts that she and her husband repeatedly told their relatives that they refused to have their children undergo these rituals because of their Christian faith and Mr. Iyere’s own negative experiences.

propositions.text: Relatives threatened children would be taken by force if refusal continued; police were unresponsive.
propositions.quote: Ms. Iyere claims that their relatives stated that, if they continued to refuse, the children would be taken by force. The local police were not responsive to their concerns.

propositions.text: Family relocated to Ibadan, then hid in a church in Lagos after a relative threatened to disclose their location.
propositions.quote: The family then relocated to the city of Ibadan. In Ibadan, they encountered a relative who stated that he would disclose their location. The family then went into hiding in a church in Lagos.

propositions.text: While hiding in Lagos, they learned Mr. Iyere’s kinsmen had come looking for them there.
propositions.quote: While in hiding, they were informed that Mr. Iyere’s kinsmen had come looking for them there.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Iyere says they refused rituals for faith reasons, faced threats, police unresponsive, relocated and hid, with kinsmen searching for them.

propositions.text: Applicants arrived in Canada Sept 9, 2016; Mr. Iyere stayed in Nigeria and returned to Ibadan.
propositions.quote: The Applicants left Nigeria and arrived in Canada on September 9, 2016. Mr. Iyere remained in Nigeria and returned to Ibadan.

propositions.text: Ms. Iyere was told kinsmen searched for children in Ibadan and community members were told to look everywhere in Nigeria.
propositions.quote: Ms. Iyere recounts that she was told that Mr. Iyere’s kinsmen came looking for the children in Ibadan and that their community association members had been told to look for them everywhere in Nigeria.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants arrived in Canada; Mr. Iyere stayed in Nigeria; Ms. Iyere says kinsmen searched for children widely in Nigeria.

propositions.text: RPD found Ms. Iyere credible with subjective fear but fear not objectively well-founded.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Protection Division [RPD] found that Ms. Iyere’s testimony was credible and that she had a subjective fear of persecution in Nigeria, but that her fear was not objectively well-founded.

propositions.text: RPD found Applicants had an IFA in Port Harcourt and could relocate safely and reasonably.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the Applicants had an IFA in Port Harcourt and that they could relocate there safely and reasonably.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found Ms. Iyere credible but fear not objectively well-founded; found Applicants had safe, reasonable IFA in Port Harcourt.

propositions.text: RPD found encounter with relative in Ibadan was coincidence.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the family’s encounter with a relative in Ibadan was a coincidence.

propositions.text: RPD found Lagos encounter did not prove community could locate them anywhere; possibly Mr. Iyere’s mother disclosed location.
propositions.quote: The RPD further found that the encounter in Lagos did not demonstrate the ability of their community association members to locate them anywhere in Nigeria; rather, it was possible that Mr. Iyere’s mother provided their location, given that she is supportive of the rituals.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found Ibadan encounter coincidental and Lagos encounter did not prove community could find them; possibly mother disclosed location.

propositions.text: RPD found Port Harcourt valid IFA due to size and distance from other locations.
propositions.quote: The RPD considered Port Harcourt’s size, as a city of 2 million inhabitants, and its distance from Lagos, Ibadan, and Mr. Iyere’s home town, and found it to be a valid IFA.

propositions.text: RPD found Applicants would not face undue hardship relocating due to successful careers and being well-off.
propositions.quote: The RPD also found that the Applicants would not be subject to undue hardship in relocating to Port Harcourt because Ms. Iyere and her husband had successful careers and were reasonably well-off.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found Port Harcourt a valid IFA and relocation not unduly hard given Applicants' careers and financial status.

propositions.text: RPD concluded Applicants did not establish serious possibility of persecution or risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment throughout Nigeria.
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that the Applicants had not established that they faced a serious possibility of persecution throughout Nigeria or that they would face a danger of torture, a risk to life, or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment throughout Nigeria.

paragraphs.summary: RPD concluded Applicants failed to prove serious risk of persecution or harm throughout Nigeria.

propositions.text: RAD conducted appeal of RPD decision guided by Huruglica principles and independently assessed evidence.
propositions.quote: The RAD conducted the appeal of the RPD’s decision guided by the principles set out in Huruglica v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2014 FC 799, [2014] 4 FCR 811, and independently assessed the evidence.

propositions.text: RAD dismissed appeal and confirmed RPD decision.
propositions.quote: The RAD dismissed the appeal and confirmed the decision of the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: RAD independently reviewed and dismissed appeal, confirming RPD decision.

propositions.text: RAD applied two-part test for IFA reasonableness from Rasaratnam and Thirunavukkarasu.
propositions.quote: The RAD applied the two part test to determine the reasonableness of the proposed IFA, citing Rasaratnam v Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration), [1992] 1 FC 706, [1991] FCJ No 1256 (QL) (FCA) [Rasaratnam], and Thirunavukkarasu v Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration), [1994] 1 FC 589, [1993] FCJ No 1172 (QL) (FCA) [Thirunavukkarasu].

paragraphs.summary: RAD applied two-part test for IFA reasonableness from precedent cases Rasaratnam and Thirunavukkarasu.

propositions.text: RAD agreed with RPD that less than mere possibility Applicants would be found if relocated to Port Harcourt.
propositions.quote: The RAD agreed with the RPD that there was less than a mere possibility that Ms. Iyere and her children would be found if they relocated to Port Harcourt.

propositions.text: RAD considered Nigeria's population, Port Harcourt's population, distance, and poor communications infrastructure in analysis.
propositions.quote: The RAD considered, among other things, the overall population of Nigeria (180 million) and of Port Harcourt (2 million), the distance between Port Harcourt and the Applicants’ home, and the information in the National Documentation Package [NDP] indicating that the communications infrastructure in Nigeria is generally poor.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found low chance of being found in Port Harcourt, considering population, distance, and poor communications.

propositions.text: RAD found fear of forced FGM not well-founded given recent country documents showing law enforcement against FGM.
propositions.quote: The RAD found that Ms. Iyere’s fear that her daughter would be taken by force and subjected to FGM was not well-founded in light of the more recent country condition documents that established, among other things, that the practice is contrary to national law and the law is being enforced.

propositions.text: RAD found no support for Applicants' claim children would be taken by force if parents refuse FGM.
propositions.quote: The RAD found nothing to support the Applicants’ contention that the children would be taken by force if their parents refuse to have them undergo FGM.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found fear of forced FGM not well-founded and no evidence children would be taken by force if parents refuse.

propositions.text: Applicants alleged RPD's IFA reasonableness analysis was too brief, lacked detail, and ignored personal circumstances including mental health.
propositions.quote: The RAD considered the Applicants’ allegations that the RPD’s analysis of the reasonableness of the proposed relocation was too brief, lacked detail, and failed to address their personal circumstances including Ms. Iyere’s mental health.

propositions.text: RAD agreed with RPD that given Applicants' profile, relocation to Port Harcourt was not unreasonable.
propositions.quote: However, the RAD ultimately agreed with the RPD that, given the particular profile of Ms. Iyere and her husband, who both had careers, had travelled and were well-off, relocation to Port Harcourt was not unreasonable.

propositions.text: RAD concluded Applicants were not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection individually or collectively.
propositions.quote: The RAD concluded that the Applicants were not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection, either individually or collectively.

paragraphs.summary: RAD considered Applicants' complaints about RPD's analysis but agreed relocation was reasonable and Applicants not refugees or in need of protection.

propositions.text: Issue is whether RAD erred in finding IFA reasonable, the determinative finding of RPD and RAD.
propositions.quote: The only issue is whether the RAD erred in finding that the IFA is reasonable, as this was the determinative finding of both the RPD and the RAD.

paragraphs.summary: Court states issue is whether RAD erred in finding IFA reasonable, the key finding of RPD and RAD.

propositions.text: RAD's IFA analysis is reviewed on reasonableness standard per Ugbekile v Canada.
propositions.quote: The determination of the RAD regarding an IFA analysis is reviewed on the standard of reasonableness: Ugbekile v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2016 FC 1397 at paras 12-14, 275 ACWS (3d) 360.

paragraphs.summary: Court states RAD's IFA analysis is reviewed on reasonableness standard per Ugbekile v Canada.

propositions.text: Reasonableness review considers justification, transparency, intelligibility, and if decision is defensible on facts and law per Dunsmuir.
propositions.quote: Where the reasonableness standard applies, the Court considers “the existence of justification, transparency and intelligibility within the decision-making process” and “whether the decision falls within a range of possible, acceptable outcomes which are defensible in respect of the facts and law”: Dunsmuir v New Brunswick, 2008 SCC 9 at para 47, [2008] 1 SCR 190.

paragraphs.summary: Court explains reasonableness review considers justification, transparency, intelligibility, and defensibility per Dunsmuir.

propositions.text: Applicants argue RAD erred applying two-part IFA reasonableness test from Rasaratnam.
propositions.quote: The Applicants submit that the RAD erred in its application of the two part test to determine the reasonableness of an IFA as established in Rasaratnam.

propositions.text: Applicants argue RAD erred in analyzing serious risk of persecution and reasonableness of IFA in their personal circumstances.
propositions.quote: The Applicants submit that the RAD erred both in its analysis of the whether there was a serious risk of persecution throughout the country and in its analysis of whether the proposed IFA was reasonable in their personal circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue RAD erred applying two-part IFA test, both on risk of persecution and IFA reasonableness in their circumstances.

propositions.text: Applicants say RAD disregarded Ms. Iyere’s credible testimony about husband's family network to find children.
propositions.quote: The Applicants submit that the RAD disregarded Ms. Iyere’s testimony about the breadth of her husband’s family’s network and how they could use this network and their community association meetings to find her children.

propositions.text: Applicants say RPD and RAD should have accepted Ms. Iyere’s credible testimony without more evidence.
propositions.quote: The Applicants submit that the RPD and RAD found Ms. Iyere to be credible and should have accepted this testimony without additional evidence.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue RAD disregarded credible testimony about family network and should have accepted it without more evidence.

propositions.text: Applicants argue RAD selectively used NDP evidence on FGM prevalence in Nigeria including Port Harcourt.
propositions.quote: The Applicants also argue that the RAD was selective in its use of the NDP evidence relating to FGM.

propositions.text: Applicants provided evidence that FGM is prevalent throughout Nigeria including Port Harcourt and community can use force if parents refuse.
propositions.quote: The Applicants note that they provided evidence that FGM is prevalent throughout Nigeria, including in the Port Harcourt region, and that the newspaper article submitted demonstrates that the community can use force when parents do not consent to FGM.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue RAD selectively used evidence on FGM prevalence and that FGM is prevalent including in Port Harcourt with force used if parents refuse.

propositions.text: The RAD made factual errors and did not fully analyze their particular circumstances.
propositions.quote: the Applicants submit that the RAD made factual errors which demonstrate that the RAD did not fully analyze their particular circumstances

propositions.text: The RAD inaccurately stated Ms. Iyere had post-secondary education and claimed not to speak Esan/Ishan language.
propositions.quote: the RAD inaccurately stated that Ms. Iyere had a post-secondary education and that she claimed not to speak the Esan/Ishan language

paragraphs.summary: The Applicants argue the RAD made factual errors and mischaracterized Ms. Iyere's education and language skills.

propositions.text: The RAD erred in rejecting Ms. Iyere’s psychotherapist’s report noting mental health risks.
propositions.quote: the Applicants also argue that the RAD erred in rejecting Ms. Iyere’s psychotherapist’s report, which noted the risks to her mental health

paragraphs.summary: The Applicants argue the RAD wrongly rejected a psychotherapist's report about Ms. Iyere's mental health risks.

propositions.text: The RAD did not consider their risk of kidnapping in Port Harcourt, where they would be more visible and vulnerable due to wealth.
propositions.quote: the Applicants submit that the RAD did not consider their risk of kidnapping in Port Harcourt. They now argue that they would be more visible as strangers in Port Harcourt and more vulnerable to kidnapping given their wealth

paragraphs.summary: The Applicants argue the RAD failed to consider their kidnapping risk in Port Harcourt due to visibility and wealth.

propositions.text: The RAD applied the correct two part test and its finding is reasonable.
propositions.quote: The Respondent submits that the RAD applied the correct two part test and its finding is reasonable

paragraphs.summary: The Respondent submits the RAD applied the correct test and its decision is reasonable.

propositions.text: The RAD considered the Applicants’ fear of being found in Port Harcourt but found little objective evidence of community reach and power, making the fear unlikely.
propositions.quote: The RAD did not ignore the Applicants’ fear that Mr. Iyere’s family, community members, or kinsmen would find them in Port Harcourt but, rather, found that there was little objective evidence regarding the size, reach, and power of this community

paragraphs.summary: The Respondent says the RAD considered but found little objective evidence supporting the Applicants' fear of being found in Port Harcourt.

propositions.text: The RAD made no negative credibility findings but found evidence insufficient; subjective fear accepted but well-foundedness requires objective evidence.
propositions.quote: The Respondent notes that the RAD, like the RPD, did not make any negative credibility findings, but rather found that the evidence was not sufficient or probative

paragraphs.summary: The Respondent notes the RAD accepted subjective fear but found insufficient objective evidence and made no negative credibility findings.

propositions.text: The RAD erred on Ms. Iyere’s education and language but this does not affect decision reasonableness given other evidence of their status.
propositions.quote: The Respondent acknowledges that the RAD erred in stating Ms. Iyere’s level of education and language spoken, but submits that this does not impact the reasonableness of the decision

paragraphs.summary: The Respondent acknowledges errors about Ms. Iyere’s education and language but says it does not affect the decision's reasonableness.

propositions.text: The RAD did not err rejecting the psychotherapist’s report; no specific RPD errors raised; report lacks impact on mental health in IFA; no evidence of significant hardship.
propositions.quote: The Respondent further submits that the RAD did not err in its treatment of the psychotherapist’s report

paragraphs.summary: The Respondent argues the RAD properly rejected the psychotherapist’s report due to lack of specific errors and insufficient evidence of hardship.

propositions.text: Applicants did not provide sufficient evidence of life or safety jeopardy in the IFA as required by Ranganathan.
propositions.quote: With respect to the claimed risk of kidnapping, the Respondent submits that the Applicants did not provide sufficient evidence of conditions that would jeopardize their lives or safety in the proposed IFA

paragraphs.summary: The Respondent submits the Applicants failed to provide sufficient evidence of life or safety risk in the IFA as required by precedent.

propositions.text: The two part IFA test requires no serious possibility of persecution and unreasonableness of seeking refuge there considering all circumstances.
propositions.quote: The two part test for an IFA was set out in Thirunavukkarasu and reflects the principles previously established in Rasaratnam

paragraphs.summary: The court states the two part test for an IFA from Thirunavukkarasu and Rasaratnam.

propositions.text: An IFA must be realistic and accessible; claimants cannot face great danger or undue hardship to reach or stay there.
propositions.quote: An IFA cannot be speculative or theoretical only; it must be a realistic, attainable option

paragraphs.summary: The court quotes Thirunavukkarasu explaining that an IFA must be realistic and accessible without undue hardship.

propositions.text: High threshold for unreasonableness requires conditions jeopardizing life or safety with concrete evidence; absence of relatives insufficient alone.
propositions.quote: It requires nothing less than the existence of conditions which would jeopardize the life and safety of a claimant in travelling or temporarily relocating to a safe area

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Ranganathan setting a high threshold for unreasonableness requiring concrete evidence of life or safety jeopardy.

propositions.text: The onus is on applicants to establish with objective evidence that relocation to IFA is unreasonable; not on the Board to prove reasonableness.
propositions.quote: Whether the relocation to the IFA is unreasonable is an objective test and the onus is on the applicants to establish on objective evidence that the relocation to the IFA is unreasonable

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Argote confirming applicants bear the onus to prove unreasonableness of relocation to IFA with objective evidence.

propositions.text: Claimant must prove serious possibility of persecution or unreasonableness of seeking refuge in IFA on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: The claimant must persuade the Board on a balance of probabilities either that there is a serious possibility that he or she will be persecuted in the location proposed by the Board as an IFA, or that it would be unreasonable to seek refugee in the proposed IFA

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Valasquez summarizing the claimant's burden to prove serious risk or unreasonableness of the IFA.

propositions.text: Refugee claimants must show with objective evidence that IFA is unreasonable due to serious risk or conditions jeopardizing life or safety.
propositions.quote: The refugee claimant bears the onus of establishing with objective evidence that the IFA is unreasonable; i.e., that there is a serious possibility of the claimant being persecuted in the proposed IFA or that the conditions in the proposed IFA make it unreasonable

paragraphs.summary: The court states the high threshold for proving IFA unreasonableness requires objective evidence of serious risk or jeopardizing conditions.

propositions.text: The RAD applied the correct test and did not err in finding the Applicants failed to prove the IFA in Port Harcourt is unreasonable.
propositions.quote: The RAD applied the correct test and did not err in finding that the Applicants had not met the onus on them to establish on a balance of probabilities that the IFA in Port Harcourt is not reasonable

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RAD correctly applied the test and did not err in finding the IFA reasonable.

propositions.text: The RAD focused on likelihood of being found in the IFA and found Applicants lacked objective evidence of community reach or authority.
propositions.quote: the RAD’s analysis of whether the family was at a serious risk of persecution throughout the country focused on whether it was likely they would be found in the proposed IFA

propositions.text: Credible testimony does not replace need for objective evidence to prove IFA unreasonableness.
propositions.quote: the fact that their testimony was found to be credible with respect to their fear does not alleviate the need to provide sufficient objective evidence

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RAD reasonably required objective evidence beyond credible testimony to assess risk in the IFA.

propositions.text: The RAD reasonably found encounters in Ibadan and Lagos were coincidental and did not prove community capacity to locate Applicants.
propositions.quote: The RAD reasonably found that the encounters in Ibadan and Lagos were coincidental and/or due to information provided by Mr. Iyere’s mother

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RAD reasonably concluded encounters were coincidental and did not show community capacity to find Applicants.

propositions.text: The RAD reasonably concluded less than a mere possibility of Applicants being found in Port Harcourt and facing claimed risks.
propositions.quote: The RAD reasonably concluded, based on the geographic factors and the country condition documents and the other evidence provided, that there was less than a mere possibility of the Applicants being found in Port Harcourt and facing the risks they claimed

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RAD reasonably concluded a low likelihood of Applicants being found and facing risks in Port Harcourt.

propositions.text: The RAD acknowledged FGM prevalence but found no evidence children would be forcibly taken if parents opposed; gave little weight to opinion article.
propositions.quote: the RAD found that the documents relied on by the Applicants did not demonstrate that girls would be taken by force for FGM if both of their parents opposed the practice

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RAD reasonably gave little weight to evidence about forced FGM against parental wishes.

propositions.text: Poor communications infrastructure in Nigeria poses risks as Applicants cannot contact police if needed
propositions.quote: the poor communications infrastructure in Nigeria would pose other risks because the Applicants would not be able to contact the police if needed

propositions.text: Ms. Iyere's public work increases likelihood community members will find her
propositions.quote: because Ms. Iyere works in the public as a tailor and clothes-trader, it is more probable that people from her community will find her

propositions.text: RPD and RAD were not provided objective evidence supporting new or previous submissions about IFA unreasonableness or risk
propositions.quote: The RPD and RAD were not provided with any evidence by the Applicants which would have objectively supported these new submissions or those previously made

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues poor communications and Ms. Iyere's public work increase risks; earlier decision-maker found no objective evidence supporting these claims.

propositions.text: Second prong of test requires objective evidence to show IFA is unreasonable considering personal circumstances
propositions.quote: The onus is on the Applicants to provide objective evidence to establish that the IFA is not reasonable for them

paragraphs.summary: Court states Applicants must provide objective evidence to prove IFA is unreasonable considering personal circumstances.

propositions.text: Factual errors by RAD about Ms. Iyere's education and language are immaterial to IFA assessment
propositions.quote: the factual errors made by the RAD regarding Ms. Iyere’s education and language spoken are not material to its assessment of the IFA

propositions.text: RAD misstated Ms. Iyere’s education but accurately analyzed family’s careers and finances, considering personal circumstances
propositions.quote: the RAD’s analysis of Ms. Iyere’s career as a tailor and clothes-trader, her husband’s career as an engineer, and the couple’s financial status were factually accurate

paragraphs.summary: Respondent says RAD's factual errors are immaterial; court finds RAD accurately considered family circumstances.

propositions.text: Applicants did not submit to RAD how RPD erred on psychotherapist’s report; RAD considered report briefly
propositions.quote: the Applicants did not make submissions to the RAD about how the RPD erred in its treatment of this evidence. Nonetheless, the RAD considered the report, albeit briefly

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Applicants did not argue RPD erred on psychotherapist report; RAD considered it briefly.

propositions.text: RAD found psychotherapist’s opinion on Ms. Iyere returning to Nigeria overstepped jurisdiction and should summarize condition only
propositions.quote: The RAD found that the psychotherapist’s opinion with respect to Ms. Iyere returning to Nigeria overstepped the psychotherapist’s jurisdiction and commented that the Report should be a summary of Ms. Iyere’s condition

paragraphs.summary: Earlier decision-maker found psychotherapist’s opinion overstepped jurisdiction, should only summarize condition.

propositions.text: Court finds RAD’s statement on psychotherapist’s report not entirely accurate or fair but RAD did not err in treatment or conclusion
propositions.quote: this is not an entirely accurate or fair statement of the contents or purpose of the psychotherapist’s report... The RAD did not err in its treatment of the report or in its conclusion that the IFA was reasonable

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD’s statement on psychotherapist report unfair but no error in treatment or conclusion on IFA reasonableness.

propositions.text: Expert opinion is only as valid as truth of facts it is based on; psychological reports do not confirm claimant allegations
propositions.quote: opinion evidence is only as valid as the truth of the facts upon which it is based... an expert report cannot confirm allegations made by a claimant

propositions.text: RPD may discount psychological evidence that merely regurgitates claimant’s reasons for stress
propositions.quote: It is within the RPD’s mandate to discount psychological evidence when the doctor merely regurgitates what the patient says are the reasons for his stress

paragraphs.summary: Prior cases hold expert opinion depends on factual truth; RPD may discount psychological evidence repeating claimant’s reasons.

propositions.text: Psychological reports advocating as opinions settling tribunal issues deserve little weight without probing
propositions.quote: psychological reports that advocate in the guise of an opinion and “propose to settle important issues to be decided by the tribunal”... little weight should be attached

paragraphs.summary: Prior authority cautions psychological reports advocating tribunal issues deserve little weight without probing.

propositions.text: RAD may scrutinize psychological reports and discount opinions on issues decision-maker must decide
propositions.quote: The RAD is entitled to scrutinize psychological reports and discount opinions on the issues that it or the RPD, as the decision-maker, should make

paragraphs.summary: Court states RAD may scrutinize and discount psychological opinions on issues it must decide.

propositions.text: Psychotherapist’s report aimed to describe Ms. Iyere’s mental health to support relevance to IFA reasonableness, not credibility
propositions.quote: the psychotherapist’s report was not offered to buttress the credibility of the Applicants’ allegations, but to describe Ms. Iyere’s mental health

paragraphs.summary: Court finds psychotherapist report described mental health to support IFA relevance, not credibility.

propositions.text: Psychotherapist’s report dated Nov 2016 describes Ms. Iyere’s anxiety and depression but does not focus on IFA
propositions.quote: The Report is dated November 28, 2016... The Report notes that she has anxiety and depression and that she reports sleeplessness and other cognitive impacts

propositions.text: Report concludes Ms. Iyere’s return to Nigeria could worsen mental and physical stress symptoms
propositions.quote: I believe that Mrs. Iyere’s return to Nigeria could cause her mental and physical stress symptoms to increase considerably

paragraphs.summary: Court notes psychotherapist report describes anxiety and depression, concludes return to Nigeria could worsen symptoms.

propositions.text: Psychotherapist’s opinion is within mental health role; RAD must weigh report’s relevance to IFA reasonableness
propositions.quote: it is the role of the RAD to consider the Report and determine the extent to which it is relevant to the reasonableness of the proposed IFA

paragraphs.summary: Court states psychotherapist’s opinion is proper; RAD must assess report’s relevance to IFA reasonableness.

propositions.text: In Olalere, Justice Russell found IFA unreasonable due to RAD’s failure to consider psychological evidence
propositions.quote: Justice Russell found that a proposed IFA was not reasonable based on the RAD’s failure to consider the psychological evidence

paragraphs.summary: Prior case found IFA unreasonable because RAD failed to consider psychological evidence.

propositions.text: Justice Russell noted psychological evidence is central to IFA reasonableness and cannot be disregarded
propositions.quote: psychological evidence is central to the question of whether the IFA is reasonable and cannot be disregarded

propositions.text: Justice Brown in Asif found psychologist reports relevant but dismissed application due to report flaws
propositions.quote: psychologist reports are relevant in an IFA analysis... Justice Brown ultimately dismissed the application because the RAD was reasonable in finding various issues with the report

propositions.text: In present case, RAD failed to engage psychological report or provide reasons for dismissal unlike Asif
propositions.quote: in the present case, the RAD fails to engage the report at all, let alone provide reasonable reasons for its dismissal

paragraphs.summary: Prior cases hold psychological evidence central to IFA; present case differs as RAD engaged report unlike Asif.

propositions.text: Jurisprudence cautions on psychological reports based on claimant accounts but error is RAD’s failure to address report
propositions.quote: jurisprudence has noted the need for caution in assessing psychological reports... error of the RAD was in failing to deal with the psychologist’s report

paragraphs.summary: Jurisprudence cautions on claimant-based psychological reports; error is RAD’s failure to address report.

propositions.text: RAD did not fail to deal with psychotherapist’s report and concluded report insufficient to show IFA unreasonable
propositions.quote: the RAD did not fail to deal with the psychotherapist’s report... the RAD quickly concluded that the Report was not sufficient to establish that the proposed IFA was unreasonable

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD addressed psychotherapist report and found it insufficient to prove IFA unreasonable.

propositions.text: For IFA to be unreasonable, concrete evidence of life and safety jeopardy is required
propositions.quote: for an IFA to be found to be unreasonable there must be actual and concrete evidence of conditions which would jeopardize the life and safety of the claimant

propositions.text: Psychotherapist’s report does not address worsening of Ms. Iyere’s condition if relocated to Port Harcourt
propositions.quote: The psychotherapist’s report does not address the extent to which Ms. Iyere’s anxiety and depression would worsen if relocated to Port Harcourt

propositions.text: Report focused on impact of return to Nigeria generally, not on IFA which was not proposed then
propositions.quote: The Report more generally spoke of the impact on Ms. Iyere’s if returned to Nigeria, due to her worry about her children being subjected to FGM and other rituals

paragraphs.summary: Court states IFA unreasonableness requires concrete evidence; report does not address worsening if relocated to Port Harcourt.

propositions.text: RAD reasonably concluded Applicants failed to provide clear evidence of life and safety jeopardy from kidnapping risk
propositions.quote: the RAD reasonably concluded that the Applicants had not provided clear and concrete evidence of conditions which would jeopardize their life and safety

propositions.text: Country documents on kidnappings do not constitute concrete evidence; Applicants’ kidnapping risk claim unsupported
propositions.quote: The country condition documents about the prevalence of kidnappings... do not constitute concrete evidence. Their assertion... is unsupported by any evidence

propositions.text: Risk of kidnapping is not different from past circumstances as vulnerability is due to wealth
propositions.quote: the risk of kidnapping they now assert is not different from their past circumstances, given that they claim that it is their wealth which makes them vulnerable

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD reasonably concluded no clear evidence of kidnapping risk jeopardizing Applicants’ safety.
